text:
elaine: FYI - since the VPC egress deny rolled in eu-west-1 weve seen ~18% of GPU node joins fail. error looks like KMS handshake/timeouts + audit-export 403s. rolling warm pool + new nodes both affected.
ops-bot: ALERT: keystore-proxy v2.3 handshake failure (eu-west-1) 1865432115 - 52 errors in 10m :rotating_light:
chris: thanks. any correlation with the new keystore IAM condition that blocks access from nat-gw IPs?
mira: yes, the new IAM binding added a source VPC condition yesterday afternoon for compliance. audit export for the new keystore is routed through our NATs.
elaine: i pulled a node bootstrap log: 
```
ERROR: unable to decrypt key: AccessDeniedException (kms:Decrypt) 
	at keystore proxy -> auditshipper -> s3 (403)
CausedBy: principal condition sourceip mismatch
```
chris: that matches. nodes use ephemeral sts role -> keystore grant. the grant is fine, but the keystore IAM condition expects traffic from private-link in prod, not nat.
jonah: compliance asked for keystore audit exports to always originate from managed NATs so we have fixed egress IPs for SIEM ingestion. changing that was the reason for the source-ip condition.
elaine: problem: GPU onboarding depends on keystore decrypt during kubelet start. if we whitelist NATs for the keystore grant we re-open broad egress window for other services and blow our audit isolation story.
mira: we need a short-term mitigation that doesn't weaken the audit policy. options: 1) temporary keystore grant exception for the gpu-onboard role with short TTL 2) route only the warm-pool /provision subnets through privatelink to keystore 3) fallback to local ephemeral keys cached on warm-pool (but requires regen + some code change).
chris: quick cost note: routing eu-west warm-pool via NATs -> increase natgw data charges ~€1200/day at current surge. privatelink setup ~1-2 day ops + small cross-account endpoint fee but lower transfer costs.
elaine: can we do (1) + (2) together: short-term grant exception for 4 hours to drain onboarding backlog, and meanwhile provision privatelink for warm-pool subnets as canonical fix?
jonah: security sign-off: short exception ok if scoped to the role Arn: `arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/gpu-onboard` and add an automated revoke job in 4h. must be logged in ticket: INFSEC-3982.
mira: also ensure auditshipper will record the grant creation and revocation. retention for these logs must be at least 90d per policy.
chris: implement plan: 
- elaine: kick off the 4h grant (i can do a terraform patch to add conditional exception)
- ops: create privatelink endpoint and route table entries for warm-pool subnets (target: canary within 3h)
- infra-sre: monitor node-joins, target <5% join-fail by end of rotation

elaine: terraform snippet ill apply (will PR):
```hcl
resource "aws_iam_policy_document" "gpu_onboard_keystore_exception" {
  statement {
    actions = ["kms:Decrypt"]
    resources = ["arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01"]
    principals { type = "AWS" identifiers = ["arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/gpu-onboard"] }
    condition {
      test = "StringEquals"
      variable = "aws:SourceIp"
      values = ["54.12.34.56/32"]
    }
    sid = "short-lived-gpu-onboard-exception"
  }
}
```
mira: set ops-bot to post the revoke at +4h and add a pager duty alert if revoke fails.
ops-bot: scheduled job created: revoke-keystore-exception @ 4h from 1865432115. will post status.
chris: monitoring queries to watch: 
- node.bootstrap.failures.count by az
- keystore.decrypt.403.rate
- natgw egress bytes & cost estimate
- auditshipper.s3.put.failures

elaine: one more cost tradeoff: if we keep the privatelink long-term, we pay endpoint hours + cross-AZ data but drop persistent natgw costs. estimate: break-even ~12 days at current load.
jonah: compliance note: update the control doc (controls/keystore-egress.md) with the temporary exception and link INFSEC-3982. we need a post-mortem if this repeats.
chris: ok i'll run the monitoring dashboard and post a short deck for leadership if this touches >500 nodes.
elaine: ill open the PR and ping reviewers. rolling the grant now will be last-resort; trying a canary with privatelink first if we can get endpoint up quick.
mira: agree. prioritise privatelink canary + low-scope grant as fallback. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: NOTE: keystore-proxy deploy v2.3 -> v2.4 planned at 1865434000, consider delaying if nodes still failing.
